title: US Sens. Warren, Blumenthal, Van Hollen issue report on data center practices
source_used: Market Briefs (briefs.co); MLex original is paywalled
key_facts: A Friday report (9 Oct 2026) by Sens. Elizabeth Warren (MA), Chris Van Hollen (MD) and Richard Blumenthal (CT) says state and local data centre tax incentives cost governments billions in revenue.
The report says Big Tech benefits while 'ratepayers, taxpayers, and local communities' shoulder many of the costs and that the companies 'are not doing enough to pay their fair share'.
The authors say the conditions attached to the exemptions, such as adding permanent jobs or supplying dedicated power, set a low bar that is often easily met.
Warren and other Senate Democrats have already pressed Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet for details on how tax breaks financed their data centre buildouts.
MLex's headline: 'US Sens. Warren, Blumenthal, Van Hollen issue report on data center practices' (article paywalled; only the headline was readable).
quote_evidence: According to the authors, the exemptions data center developers use often come with conditions like adding permanent jobs or supplying their own dedicated power, but "the qualifications set such a low bar that they can often be met with relative ease."
why_it_matters_hint: New evidence on who pays for data centre incentives, from three Democratic senators.
notes: MLex (the pool item) is paywalled, so the text was read at Market Briefs, which does not name where the report can be found. Whether this is the same document that TIME previewed on 8 Oct is not stated.
